subject_entity.notes: Prophetic movement originating in Phrygia c. 170 under Montanus, Priscilla, and Maximilla; emphasized ongoing prophecy, strict asceticism, and rigorist discipline; spread across Asia, Rome, and North Africa; Tertullian later joined their cause.

object_entity.notes: Major North African city; center of Latin Christianity from Tertullian through Cyprian and Augustine; seat of important regional councils.

passage.excerpt: Marcion of Pontus succeeded [Cerdo] and developed his doctrine, blaspheming with shameless effrontery Him proclaimed as God by the law and the prophets, declaring Him the author of evils, taking delight in war, infirm of purpose, and contrary to Himself. But Jesus, derived from that father above the God who made the world, came into Judaea in the times of Pontius Pilate, was manifested in the form of a man — abolishing the prophets and the law — but not truly taking flesh. He also mutilated the Gospel according to Luke, removing all that is written respecting the generation of the Lord.
